content.value_statement: Database changes can break production data when migrations are incomplete or irreversible. This skill drafts migration steps, rollbacks, and review checklists for common SQL and ORM stacks.
actual_capabilities: Drafts forward and rollback migrations for tables, columns, indexes, and foreign keys.
Shows examples for Prisma, TypeORM, Alembic, Django, Rails, Laravel, Go, and SQL tools.
Suggests staged patterns for zero-downtime column adds, renames, and removals.
Includes checklist items for backups, staging tests, reversibility, and performance review.
Provides troubleshooting patterns for failed migrations and large table updates.
limitations: Does not inspect a live database unless the user provides schema details.
Generated migrations must be reviewed against the target database and ORM version.
Examples may need syntax changes for project-specific naming and configuration.
Data migrations can still cause loss when assumptions about existing data are wrong.

use_cases.title: Add Application Features
use_cases.description: Plan new tables, columns, indexes, and rollback steps before adding product functionality.

use_cases.title: Review Risky Schema Changes
use_cases.description: Check destructive changes for reversibility, locking risk, staging tests, and backup requirements.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Release Migrations
use_cases.description: Create staged migration plans that align database changes with application deployments.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use migration-generator to add a nullable phone column to users. Include forward steps, rollback steps, and review notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create an ORM Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use migration-generator for a Prisma migration that adds user_profiles linked to users. Include constraints, indexes, and rollback guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Zero-Downtime Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use migration-generator to rename users.email to users.email_address with zero downtime. Include deployment phases and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Large Data Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use migration-generator to convert product prices from decimal dollars to integer cents in PostgreSQL. Include batching, validation, rollback limits, and monitoring.

output: Adds the email_verified field in a staged way.
Backfills existing rows before requiring a value.
Applies a default for future rows.
Includes rollback notes for removing the field.

output_examples.input: Create user profiles linked to users.
output: Creates a user_profiles table with a user relationship.
Adds uniqueness for one profile per user.
Adds supporting indexes for lookup speed.
Flags cascade behavior for review before production.
Uses a backfill phase before switching reads.
Delays the destructive drop until the old path is unused.

best_practices: Provide current schema, desired schema, database engine, ORM, and production constraints.
Ask for rollback steps and data validation checks before applying any generated migration.
Test generated migrations on a copied database or staging environment before production.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated migrations directly against production without review.
Do not combine unrelated schema changes into one large migration.
Do not skip backups, lock analysis, or rollback planning for destructive changes.

faq.question: Does it run migrations for me?
faq.answer: No. It drafts migration code and steps. You decide when and where to run them.

faq.question: Which frameworks can it help with?
faq.answer: It covers raw SQL, Prisma, TypeORM, Sequelize, Knex.js, Alembic, Django, Rails, Go tools, Laravel, and Doctrine.

faq.question: Can it create zero-downtime plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests staged adds, backfills, dual writes, and delayed drops when you provide deployment constraints.

faq.question: Can it migrate production data safely?
faq.answer: It can propose safer patterns, but production data changes still need backups, testing, monitoring, and approval.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide current schema, desired changes, database engine, ORM, table sizes, constraints, and rollback requirements.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
